sections.title: Your mission
sections.body: Learn the fictional Pulse API well enough to plan a reliable integration.

sections.title: Pulse API quickstart
sections.content: Pulse accepts events through POST /v1/events. Each request needs an Authorization bearer token and a unique Idempotency-Key. Successful acceptance returns 202 with an event_id; processing is asynchronous and is not complete at acceptance. Query GET /v1/events/{event_id} until status is processed or failed. The API allows 60 requests per minute and returns 429 with Retry-After when the limit is exceeded. Temporary unavailability returns 503 and may also include Retry-After; that response does not by itself mean the client exceeded a rate limit. A Retry-After value uses either delay seconds or an HTTP-date. Reusing an idempotency key returns the original event rather than creating a duplicate.

provenance.adaptationNote: API product names, endpoints, headers, identifiers, rate limits and metrics are fictional training data; only HTTP status-code and Retry-After semantics are referenced from the cited RFCs.

exercises.question: Why must the client query event status?
options: A 202 response means processing is asynchronous.
correctAnswer: A 202 response means processing is asynchronous.
exercises.explanation: Acceptance and final processing are separate states.

performanceTask.title: Explain and plan the integration
performanceTask.scenario: A teammate will implement Pulse tomorrow and needs your English mental model and plan.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Read the quickstart once, hide it, then explain how the API works and outline implementation without translating it.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Write 120–180 words: request lifecycle, idempotency, rate-limit behavior and a four-step implementation/test plan.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Pulse accepts an authenticated event and returns 202, which means the request was accepted but processing is not complete. The client should generate one idempotency key per logical event, store that key with the returned event_id and poll status until processed or failed. Reusing the same key returns the existing event instead of creating a duplicate. I would wrap the POST and GET calls first, then add bounded polling. A 429 indicates rate limiting, so the client should wait for Retry-After before another attempt. A 503 indicates temporary unavailability rather than proof of rate limiting; if Retry-After is present, the client should respect it. Finally, I would test duplicate submissions, failed processing, 429 backoff and 503 recovery before enabling real traffic.
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Rewrite the mental model in your own words and connect every implementation step to a behavior in the docs.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: A new Jobs API returns 202, exposes job status and uses request tokens for deduplication. Produce a fresh mental model and plan that separates acceptance, rate limiting and temporary unavailability.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Read an unseen API quickstart once and explain lifecycle, safety mechanism, failure handling and first implementation plan from memory.

artifacts.title: Reliability contract
artifacts.content: 202 means accepted, not processed. Store event_id and one key per logical event. Poll until processed or failed. When a 429 response includes Retry-After, wait for that interval and do not create a new key for the same logical event.

artifacts.title: Jobs quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /v2/jobs requires X-Request-Token and returns 202 with job_ref; acceptance is not completion. Query GET /v2/jobs/{job_ref} until complete or failed. Duplicate tokens return the existing job. Rate limiting returns 429 with Retry-After. Temporary unavailability returns 503 and may also include Retry-After; a 503 is not proof that the caller exceeded a rate limit.

artifacts.title: Exports quickstart
artifacts.content: POST /exports accepts a report request and returns 202 with export_id; acceptance is not completion. Supply Client-Request-Id to deduplicate. Poll /exports/{export_id}; download_url appears only at ready. On 429, wait for Retry-After before polling again.

trainingSource.title: Quanta Tasks API
trainingSource.content: POST /tasks requires Authorization and Request-Key. It returns 202 plus task_id; acceptance is not completion. Poll GET /tasks/{task_id} until done or failed. Reusing Request-Key returns the original task. When the service returns 429, wait for Retry-After.
